en.title: July Inflation Outlook Cools
en.summary: The probability of US monthly inflation increasing by 0.1% or more in July dropped by 10.5% to 56%, primarily driven by recent reports of cooling inflation in Sweden, Switzerland, and South Korea for the same month. These international trends suggest a potentially less 'hot' global inflation environment, influencing US expectations.
drivers: Swedish inflation slowed in July.
Swiss domestic prices rose only 0.1% in July.
South Korea's CPI cooled to 2.8% in July.
en.why_matters: US July inflation data is a critical input for Federal Reserve policy decisions, impacting interest rates and broader economic stability. A lower-than-expected inflation print could ease pressure for further rate hikes.
en.bull_case: Despite international cooling, some analysts predict US core CPI could still come in 'hot,' pushing the probability higher.
en.bear_case: Global disinflationary trends, as seen in Sweden and South Korea, could signal a broader slowdown in US price increases.
